*   Angular offset between disks: $360^\circ / (3 \times l)$ [S1].

The claim states that the angular offset between disks is $360^circ / (3 imes l)$. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in multiple sections. Specifically, in the notes and Section 4.3.3, it states: 'For an assembly with l layers and three blades per disk, the i-th layer is rotated by $360(i-1)/(3 imes l)[^circ]$ relative to the frontmost layer.' The base angular offset between adjacent layers (where i increments by 1) is therefore $360/(3 imes l)$. The source further validates this by calculating specific examples: 'the angular offset was 24° for the five-layer configuration ($360/(3 imes 5) = 24$) and 40° for the three-layer configuration ($360/(3 imes 3) = 40$).' Thus, every fact in the claim is present and supported by the evidence.
